sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever wished you could add or subtract 1 from a variable with just one character? That’s exactly what increment and decrement operators do!

• How `++` and `--` make your code shorter and cleaner
• The difference between `i++` and `++i` (it’s sneaky!)
• Where these operators shine in real programs

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you’re counting apples in a basket. Every time you add one apple, you could say `apples = apples + 1`. But what if you could just say `apples++`? That’s the magic of these operators!

These operators come in two flavors:
• **Postfix** (`i++`, `i--`): Use the value first, then change it
• **Prefix** (`++i`, `--i`): Change the value first, then use it

They might look similar, but they behave differently when used in expressions. Let’s break it down:

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: ++x (prefix): increments x first, then returns the new value
x++ (postfix): returns the current value of x, then increments
--x and x-- decrement in the same prefix/postfix pattern
In standalone statements (x++;), prefix and postfix have the same effect
In expressions (y = x++), the difference in evaluation order matters

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: `i++` and `++i` both add 1, but behave differently in expressions. Postfix (`i++`): use first, then change. Prefix (`++i`): change first, then use. Practice with simple examples to master the difference. Ready to use these in loops and counters next.
